evidence.reason: This is a hardening/scope-enlargement proposal, not an implementation error in existing intended behavior. `git log -p` rename detection only suppresses *unchanged* content, and unchanged content is by definition pre-existing—a pure rename cannot introduce a new secret. The scanner's added-text semantics are working as intended, and the inline comments show the deliberate threat model is revision-controlled `.gitattributes` (diff/binary/textconv/ext-diff: `--text --no-textconv --no-ext-diff`), not renames. The asserted concrete bypass—skipping the `env-file` and `agent-local-state` path rules—depends on gitleaks path-based configuration that is not present in any supplied source (no gitleaks config or additional_sources), so the actual security impact is unproven. Adding `--no-renames` would newly emit moved-but-unchanged content as added lines (risking false positives on the required `denylist` check) rather than repair a demonstrated defect. Line 105 does match the quoted `DIFF_OPTS`, but matching code alone does not establish an obligation to enlarge scan scope; no fixing commit was supplied.
